work_group_ration_rolls.observation: The scribe reads out each gang's name and the jars of barley owed it, and no crew goes short while another is fed twice.

ten_day_work_week.observation: Half the crew rests while the other half works, and every tenth day the halves change places.

graded_ration_scales.observation: A master smith draws three measures of grain to a carrier's one, and everyone knows a man's rank by his ration.

absence_reason_registers.observation: Beside each missing name the scribe writes the cause: fever, a brother's burial, brewing for the feast.

tool_issue_registers.observation: Chisels go out at dawn against a mark and come back at dusk, and a lost blade is docked from the ration.

palace_specialist_workshops.observation: Goldsmiths, joiners and perfume-makers work in adjoining rooms under one steward who holds the keys to their metal.

land_for_service_tenure.observation: The wheelwright holds a field by the river for as long as his household keeps turning out wheels for the palace.

ration_work_stoppages.observation: When the grain came late for the third month, the tomb crew sat down at the gate and would not lift a tool.
ration_work_stoppages.social_consequence: Crews now know that stopping work can bring the grain; overseers learn that late rations cost more than they save.

crew_grievance_hearings.observation: On the first day of each month the overseer sits under the awning and hears what the crews say they are owed.

forge_crew_roles.observation: The master holds the tongs and calls each blow, the striker swings, and the boy keeps the bellows breathing.
forge_crew_roles.ability_reason: Iron is worked hot and fast; a smithy runs on a fixed crew of master, striker and bellows hand.

rower_levies.observation: Lots are drawn in each village before the sailing season, and the men drawn walk down to the ships.

itinerant_craft_hire.observation: A bronze-caster from the hill towns works here from spring to harvest, then walks on with his moulds on a donkey.

public_hiring_grounds.observation: Before sunrise the idle stand by the well in the market square, and whoever needs hands comes to choose them.

silver_wage_payment.observation: The stone-cutters are paid in weighed silver now, and buy their bread from whoever sells it cheapest.
silver_wage_payment.ability_reason: Wages in weighed metal let a worker buy what he needs and let employers hire without a granary behind them.
silver_wage_payment.social_consequence: Workers paid in silver are no longer fed from the storehouse; a bad harvest raises bread prices and their hunger with it.

skill_graded_wages.observation: A master draws four weights of silver a month, a hand two and a boy one, written down so no one argues it.

underground_shift_rotation.observation: Lamps are counted down the shaft and counted back up; when the oil burns low, the next crew goes below.

term_limited_debt_labor.observation: A debtor may be made to work off what he owes, but in the sixth year he walks free whatever remains.

household_workshops_with_hands.observation: The potter's family works the wheel with two hired lads who sleep in the yard and eat at his table.

piece_rate_pay.observation: The weaver is paid by the finished bolt, and her lamp burns late whenever the rent is due.

iron_tool_work_norms.observation: With iron picks the ditch-diggers' daily stint is raised by half, and the overseers see that it is met.

porter_gangs.observation: Each ship's cargo belongs to one gang boss, whose men carry it to the warehouse at a fixed rate a jar.

measured_length_contracts.observation: The contractor is paid by the rod of wall finished, and the surveyor's cord settles every dispute.

village_labor_quotas.observation: The palace lists are gone; each village now owes so many days on the dykes and chooses among itself who goes.

journeyman_travel_circuits.observation: A young smith works a season with each master along the valley and carries every shop's tricks to the next.

settler_work_allotments.observation: Each settler's lot comes with days owed on the new town's wall and ditch before he may sow his own field.

surety_backed_work_contracts.observation: The builder names two neighbours who will pay if he leaves the job unfinished, and all three press their seals.

public_work_tenders.observation: The herald cries the temple roof for contract, and the lowest builder who can show sound guarantors wins it.
public_work_tenders.ability_reason: Open bidding brings every builder's price into the open and lets the city pay for work instead of feeding a levy.
public_work_tenders.social_consequence: Contracts go to the cheapest sound bid; a builder who cuts too close ruins himself, and a careless inspector lets a bad wall stand.

staged_work_acceptance.observation: No payment until the inspector has walked the foundation course, then again at the wall head, and again at the roof.

uniform_day_rate.observation: Citizen, stranger or bondman, every hand on the temple site draws the same silver for the same day.

late_completion_penalties.observation: The contract withholds a tenth for each month the gatehouse stands unroofed after the agreed day.

public_work_accounts.observation: Every payment on the great temple is cut into a stone slab in the square, down to the last load of rope.

trade_foremen.observation: Masons answer to the master mason and carpenters to the master carpenter, and neither gives the other's men orders.

master_builder_office.observation: One builder now holds the plan, the accounts and every trade's foreman, and answers to the council for the whole.
master_builder_office.ability_reason: Great works need one mind over the plan, the money and every trade; the master builder is that office.

volume_paid_quarrying.observation: Quarrymen are paid by the cubit of block cut clean, and the waste chips are theirs to burn for lime.

mine_lease_labor.observation: The city leases each gallery to a man who hires his own diggers and pays the city a share of the ore.
mine_lease_labor.social_consequence: Lessees answer for ore, not for the men who dig it; galleries go deeper and crews are used up faster.

large_owner_workshops.observation: The shield-maker's shop holds sixty hands, most of them bought, working under three freed overseers.

workshop_task_division.observation: In the lamp shop one man only throws, another only trims, a third only paints, and the lamps come off twice as fast.
workshop_task_division.ability_reason: Splitting one craft into many small tasks lets a large workshop turn out far more than the same hands working whole pieces.
workshop_task_division.social_consequence: Each worker learns one motion instead of a craft; output rises, but a trimmer cannot set up for himself.

animal_mill_tending.observation: A blindfolded donkey walks the millstone round all day while one boy feeds grain and sweeps up flour.

paid_rowing_crews.observation: Oarsmen draw a day's wage for every day at sea, and the benches fill without the drawing of lots.

crew_sick_funds.observation: Each man drops a small coin in the crew's jar on payday, and a man down with fever draws from it until he mends.

craft_mutual_aid_clubs.observation: The dyers' club dines together each month, and when a member dies it pays for his funeral and his widow's grain.

estate_bailiffs.observation: The owner lives in town; his bailiff wakes the gangs, counts the vines they prune and docks the slow.

harvest_gang_contracts.observation: A gang boss contracts to bring forty reapers on the first day of harvest, sealed and paid half in advance.

soldier_work_details.observation: Between campaigns the soldiers dig ditches and lay road stones, and grumble that they enlisted to fight.

works_contractor_companies.observation: Partners pool their money and their slaves to bid on the harbor works, and share whatever the contract clears.

freed_craftsman_obligations.observation: A freed goldsmith still owes his old master twenty days' work a year and a gift at the new-year festival.

conduit_maintenance_crews.observation: A standing crew walks the conduit each month, scraping lime crust from the channel and sealing leaking joints.

decreed_wage_rates.observation: The council fixes a laborer's day at a set weight of silver and fines any employer who pays less.

paid_fire_brigades.observation: Watchmen paid by the city patrol at night with buckets, hooks and wet blankets, and each ward knows its station.

bakery_mill_workforces.observation: Under one roof the donkeys turn the mills, the kneaders work the troughs and the ovens run from midnight.

sharecropping_tenancy.observation: The tenant keeps half the crop he raises; the other half goes by cart to the landlord's barn.

clock_timed_shifts.observation: When the water clock empties at the mine head, the night crew goes down and the vessel is filled again for them.

workman_stamp_marks.observation: Each tile-maker presses his own sign into the wet clay, so a bad batch can be traced to the hand that made it.

stamped_brickyard_output.observation: Every brick from the yard carries a stamp with the yard's name and the year of the magistrate who ruled it.

standing_engineer_corps.observation: A permanent company of builders marches with the army and in peacetime raises bridges and walls wherever it is sent.

posted_wage_tables.observation: Painted boards by the market gate list the day wage for a mason, a carter and a harvest hand.

putting_out_spinning.observation: The cloth merchant leaves carded wool at each farmhouse in autumn and collects the spun yarn in spring, paying by weight.
putting_out_spinning.ability_reason: Merchants who supply the fiber and buy the yarn turn every idle winter hearth into spinning capacity.
putting_out_spinning.social_consequence: Farm households come to depend on the merchant's wool and his price; when he stops coming, the winter income stops too.

state_manufactories.observation: The realm's arms works at the river town turns out shields and blades to one pattern, worked by bound craftsmen.

salaried_works_staff.observation: The water board keeps its own surveyors, plumbers and pavers on a yearly salary, whether or not a pipe has burst.

mill_operator_trade.observation: The miller now knows only his wheel: he dresses the stones, greases the gears and keeps the race clear.

trade_hall_lodging.observation: A traveling fuller can find a bed and the name of an employer at his trade's hall in any town on the coast road.

service_retirement_grants.observation: After twenty years' service a mason or soldier receives a plot on the frontier and a yoke of oxen.

coin_and_ration_wages.observation: The works pays half in coin and half in bread and oil, so a man's family eats even when prices climb.

civic_holiday_calendar.observation: The city's calendar marks each feast day on which no mason, weaver or carter may be made to work.

notarized_work_contracts.observation: Hire and apprenticeship contracts are written by a public notary, and a copy is filed at the record office.

home_farm_tenant_split.observation: The lord's own fields are worked by his tenants on set days; the rest of the week they till their own plots.

occupation_census.observation: Every household's register now names its trade, and the tax office knows how many smiths and bakers each town holds.
occupation_census.ability_reason: A register of every household's trade lets the state count, tax and requisition skills as well as heads.

maximum_wage_edicts.observation: The edict fixes the highest wage for each trade and the price of each good, and within a month the markets are empty.
maximum_wage_edicts.social_consequence: Fixed prices drive goods off the open market; sellers hide their stock and trade it quietly at the old prices.

hereditary_trade_obligation.observation: A baker's son must be a baker and a shipper's son a shipper, and none may leave the trade that feeds the city.
hereditary_trade_obligation.ability_reason: Binding key trades to families guarantees the bread, ships and arms the state cannot do without.
hereditary_trade_obligation.social_consequence: Sons inherit their fathers' trades by law; the state is supplied, but talent is trapped and resentment passes down with the trade.

licensed_guilds.observation: The city grants each craft's association a charter, and its officers answer for their members' dues and work.

land_bound_tenancy.observation: A tenant may no longer leave the estate where his father was registered; if he runs, he is brought back in chains.
land_bound_tenancy.social_consequence: Tenants are tied to the land for the tax roll; fields stay worked, but the countryside hardens into masters and bound men.

labor_dues_commutation.observation: Villages may now pay their road dues in coin, and the governor hires paid crews with the money.
